html:
Michelangelo was an Italian sculptor, painter, architect and poet of the High Renaissance, born in the Republic of Florence in 1475 and active mostly in Rome from his thirties. He carved the David, painted the Sistine Chapel ceiling and designed the dome of St Peter's Basilica.

He trained in Florence and as a teenager lived in the household of Lorenzo de' Medici, whose family ran the Medici Bank and the city. He thought of himself above all as a sculptor, freeing figures trapped in the stone.

Main works:

  • The Pietà in St Peter's, Rome (1498 to 1499), made in his early twenties.
  • David (1501 to 1504), a giant marble nude that became the symbol of Florence.
  • The Sistine Chapel ceiling (1508 to 1512) for Pope Julius II, over 300 figures, including the Creation of Adam.
  • The tomb of Julius II, with the figure of Moses, a project that dragged on for forty years.
  • The Last Judgement on the Sistine altar wall (1536 to 1541).
  • The dome of St Peter's, designed in his last years and finished after his death.

He worked in the same years as Leonardo da Vinci and Raphael, and was the first artist to have his life written while he was still alive. He died in Rome in 1564, almost 89, after the Reformation had split the Church and the Council of Trent was reshaping Catholic art; nudes in his Last Judgement were later painted over.
